generators.carrier: explicit import: finite presented carrier -> continuum Hilbert space over C (assumed, not constructed)

relations.statement: Z[i] is not a field: the Gaussian integer 2 (and any a+bi with norm not 1) has no inverse in Z[i]; the finite-report recovery yields M_n(Z[i]) and not M_n(C).
relations.hypotheses: a b : Int arbitrary Gaussian-integer components

relations.statement: No Gaussian-rational point on the unit circle solves the half-exponent (square-root) constraint 5(a^2-b^2)=3d^2 with a^2+b^2=d^2; continuous U(1) phases are not recovered from the finite carrier.
The Hilbert lift adds nothing to the finite-report predictions already fixed by the presented carrier; it is an explicit import, not a derived structure.
Selection on the finite quotient does not determine a continuum Hilbert carrier; the passage from finite quotient to continuum is a gap, not a theorem.
relations.hypotheses: finite presented carrier with finite report set

relations.statement: Mat2Int.trace and mat2Det are total on every Mat2Int built by the constructor from four integers, so (trace, det) of a constructed matrix is a well-typed pair of integers feeding the discriminant.

lemmas.statement: Z[i] is not a field, so the finite-report recovery M_n(Z[i]) is not M_n(C); the continuum Hilbert lift must be imported.
The self-adjoint integer matrix [[0,1],[1,1]] has trace 1, determinant -1, and characteristic discriminant 1^2 - 4*(-1) = 5.

5 is not the square of an integer, hence the eigenvalues (1 ± sqrt 5)/2 of [[0,1],[1,1]] lie outside Z (and outside Q(i)): a self-adjoint Gaussian-integer matrix need not have a Gaussian-integer eigenvalue.
lemmas.lean_skeleton: theorem five_not_int_square (x : Int) : x * x ≠ 5 := by sorry

lemmas.statement: There is no integer pair (a,b) with (2+0i)(a+bi) = 1, i.e. 2a = 1 has no integer solution; this is the elementary core of the Z[i] non-field obstruction.
lemmas.lean_skeleton: theorem two_not_unit_in_zi (a : Int) : 2 * a ≠ 1 := by omega

near_misses.claim: Since M_n(Z[i]) embeds in M_n(C), the continuum Hilbert space is already recovered from the finite carrier.
near_misses.rejecting_invariant: The embedding presupposes the field C and the completion; both are listed under @ASSUME, and hilbert_lift_redundancy/finite_quotient_vs_continuum_gap record the lift as an import, not a construction.

near_misses.claim: Every self-adjoint Gaussian-integer matrix has a Gaussian-integer eigenvalue, so spectral theory lives inside the finite carrier.
near_misses.rejecting_invariant: [[0,1],[1,1]] has discriminant 5; sqrt 5 is not in Q(i) (five_not_int_square / GAP-F001-S000-009).

near_misses.claim: Z[i] is a field because it is an integral domain with conjugation inverse z^{-1} = conj(z)/|z|^2.
near_misses.rejecting_invariant: Division by the norm |z|^2 is not available in Z[i] (2a = 1 has no integer solution; two_not_unit_in_zi, zi_non_field_obstruction).

near_misses.claim: Because rhoPlus2 = [[1,1],[1,1]] has integer eigenvalues 0 and 2, all presented-carrier observables have integer spectra.
near_misses.rejecting_invariant: rhoPlus2 has discriminant 4 (a perfect square); the discriminant-5 witness shows the integer-spectrum property is not an invariant of the carrier.

open_obligations: Construction of the continuum Hilbert completion from the finite presented carrier is not available in any @SRC declaration; it remains an explicit import (continuum Hilbert space, complex field C).

Exact Lean statements of fq_gap_stone_rational_rotation_infinite_order_and_zi_non_field_obstruction, qm020_thm4_hilbert_lift_redundancy and fq_prim_to_qm_selection_finite_quotient_vs_continuum_gap were only partially visible; the relations paraphrase them.
Field names of Mat2Int were not shown, so the trace/det composition lemmas are stated numerically rather than via Mat2Int.trace ⟨0,1,1,1⟩.
five_not_int_square is left with sorry; a case split on |x| ≤ 2 vs |x| ≥ 3 is the intended proof.
A Gaussian-integer (as opposed to integer) matrix type with conjugate-transpose is not in @SRC; the discriminant-5 witness is given over Z ⊂ Z[i].
